summary.title: Building a Custom LLM Evaluation Harness in Python from Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a minimal Python LLM evaluation harness with a golden dataset, an async LiteLLM inference runner, deterministic and LLM-as-a-judge scoring, and crash-safe JSONL logging.
takeaways: Build a golden dataset of 20-50 test cases drawn from real user inputs and known failure modes, each with an id, input, and expected_concept.
Run inference concurrently with an async LiteLLM runner that returns raw outputs only, keeping scoring separate.
Use a deterministic substring judge for exact checks and an LLM judge with a Pydantic schema for semantic checks.
Log raw outputs and scores to an append-only .jsonl file so you can re-score without repeating paid API calls.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a custom LLM evaluation harness in Python from scratch, organized into four modules: a golden dataset, an inference runner, a judge layer, and a logger. It uses LiteLLM for a unified model interface and Pydantic to force structured judge output, with asyncio for concurrent calls. Code samples cover each component, plus a summary function that computes pass rates from the log file. The guide ends with troubleshooting tips for score variance, rate limits, and judge cost, and suggestions for extending the harness.
